'''Julien Clinton Sprott''' (born 16 September 1942) is an emeritus professor of [[physics]] at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].

== Biography ==
Julien Clinton Sprott was born on 16 September 1942 in [[Memphis, Tennessee]].<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |last= |title=Julien Clinton Sprott Curriculum Vitae |url=https://sprott.physics.wisc.edu/vita.htm |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=sprott.physics.wisc.edu}}</ref> He graduated from [[Central High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Central High School.]]<ref>{{Cite news |date=1969-06-02 |title=PhD Awarded |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-memphis-press-scimitar-phd-awarded/209178916/ |access-date=2026-10-28 |work=The Memphis Press-Scimitar |pages=6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He earned his bachelor's degree from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] in 1964. He received his master's and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in physics from the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1966 and 1969, respectively.<ref name="Website-1" /> His professional interests are in experimental [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] and [[chaos theory]].

In 1984, the University of Wisconsin–Madison began a program called '''''The Wonders of Physics''''', which Sprott presented in a typical [[showman|travelling showman]] style to audiences of all ages. The show has been presented on the Madison campus over 300 times to a total audience of over 100,000 over a period of 40 years. His shows are available freely as [[Streaming media|streaming video]] from his website.

He is author of several fundamental books on [[Chaos theory|chaos]], among which ''Chaos and Time-Series Analysis'' and ''Elegant Chaos''.
